hints: Express the unit of resistance using potential difference and current.
One ohm is one volt per ampere.
walkthrough: Resistance is measured in ohms, and its SI unit can be written as volts per ampere.
Equivalently, an ohm is the resistance for which a 1 V potential difference produces a 1 A current.

ai_rubric.observable: Defines an ohm as a volt per ampere, including an equivalent unit expression.

hints: Both wires have the same resistivity, so compare their lengths and cross-sectional areas in R = ρL / A.
Q is half as long as P, but its diameter is twice as large, so its area is four times as large.
Combine the factors to express R_Q as a fraction of the given 12 Ω resistance of P.
walkthrough: For wires of the same material, R = ρL / A and a circular cross-sectional area is proportional to diameter squared.
P has length 2l and area πd² / 4, so R_P = ρ(2l) / (πd² / 4) = 8ρl / πd².
Q has length l and diameter 2d, so its area is π(2d)² / 4 = πd² and R_Q = ρl / πd².

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the resistance–resistivity relationship R = ρL / A.
Accounts for Q's halved length and fourfold cross-sectional area relative to P, or gives equivalent resistance expressions.
Relates Q's resistance to R_P / 8 and obtains 1.5 Ω.

hints: The two resistors are in parallel, so each has the full 15 V potential difference across it.
Find the power in each branch using P = V² / R, then add the two powers.
Use R_P = 12 Ω and the R_Q = 1.5 Ω result from part (b)(i).
walkthrough: Because P and Q are connected in parallel across the 15 V battery, each resistor has V = 15 V.
For P, P_P = V² / R_P = 15² / 12 = 18.75 W.
For Q, P_Q = V² / R_Q = 15² / 1.5 = 150 W.
Total power = 18.75 + 150 = 168.75 W, which is 170 W to two significant figures.

Obtains total power of about 170 W.

hints: First find the current in each parallel branch from the 15 V potential difference and the two resistances.
For wires of the same material, n and q cancel when comparing I = Anvq, so drift speed is proportional to I / A.
P has area πd² / 4 and Q has area πd² because its diameter is 2d.
walkthrough: Each parallel resistor has 15 V across it, so I_P = 15 / 12 = 1.25 A and I_Q = 15 / 1.5 = 10 A.
From I = Anvq, v is proportional to I / A because P and Q are made from the same material and therefore have the same n and q.
A_P = πd² / 4 and A_Q = π(2d)² / 4 = πd².
